new_premise.definition: T=arctg is the inverse of tangent restricted to (-pi/2,pi/2). D(T)=R and E(T)=(-pi/2,pi/2). Tangent increases on that interval. C=arcctg remains the seed inverse of cotangent restricted to (0,pi), with D(C)=R and E(C)=(0,pi).
new_premise.use_boundary: The exact tangent normalization must be stated in every affected learner-facing stem. This is an external visible premise, not a new seed concept or schema field. N87 block 3 is not added to concept_blocks. Underlying source paths in the projection are provenance only and were not opened.

shared_extension: The original conditional freeze defined B(x)=pi/2-C(x) in (-pi/2,pi/2), with tan(B(x))=x, and allowed T(x)=B(x)+k*pi. The released restricted-inverse definition now selects the unique member in (-pi/2,pi/2), namely k=0. This resolves the formerly conditional results only in this new snapshot; the old missing-premise records and review holds remain historical evidence.

C has all-real input domain, so input zero is not a cotangent-angle pole; its inverse output pi/2 is valid.

Equivalently C decreases and T increases, 2>1, and their inverse values at 1 are pi/4. This is an exact threshold comparison, not a invented special-angle evaluation or decimal estimate.

derivations.frozen_conditional_basis: T(x)+C(x)=pi/2+k*pi on any continuous tangent inverse branch, with the printed constant conditional on k=0.
derivations.extension: For any real x let c=C(x), so 0<c<pi and cot(c)=x. Put theta=pi/2-c; then -pi/2<theta<pi/2. Because sin(c) is nonzero, tan(theta)=cos(c)/sin(c)=cot(c)=x, including x=0 where c=pi/2 and theta=0. The newly released restricted tangent inverse is unique on this interval, so T(x)=theta. Hence T(x)+C(x)=pi/2 for every x in R. Alternatively the already frozen reciprocal-derivative reasoning gives (T+C)'=0 on R; the newly fixed T(0)=0 and unchanged C(0)=pi/2 give the constant pi/2. A zero derivative alone does not determine that constant.
derivations.domain: Both inverse input domains are R. The angle c avoids cotangent poles, theta avoids tangent poles, and neither output reaches its open-range endpoints. No division by x is used, so the proof covers x=0 without an exception.
